Richemont's strong jewellery sales weaken the case for blaming weak luxury demand. Gucci cut selected prices after its sales decline deepened in the third quarter.

→ Richemont reported strong first-half sales across its jewellery brands, giving jewellery businesses direct evidence of continued spending.

→ Gucci cut selected prices and added cheaper bags as its third-quarter sales decline deepened, giving competitors lower-priced products to watch.

→ Visa and Mastercard urged approval of a $38 billion card fee settlement, which would cap standard consumer card fees and limit those charges for retailers.

Richemont's jewellery sales show shoppers still spend on luxury. Brands blaming weak demand need to explain why that spending is passing them by.
Richemont reported strong first-half sales across its jewellery brands. Jewellery businesses have direct evidence of shopper spending in their own category.

Gucci cut prices on selected products and added cheaper bags after its third-quarter sales decline deepened. Its performance offers jewellery businesses a limited guide to demand for their own products.
Visa and Mastercard urged approval of a $38 billion swipe fee settlement. The deal would cap fees on standard consumer cards, giving retailers a ceiling on those charges if approved.

Gap’s sales at established stores grew for the 12th straight quarter. Warm weather hampered Old Navy’s recovery.
Walmart's Q3 revenue rose 5.2% to $188.84 billion. Online sales and advertising helped drive the retailer's growth, supporting a higher full-year forecast.
Swiss watch exports rose 9.1% to 2.46 billion francs in October, their fifth straight month of growth. Luxury retailers now have a longer run of export gains to weigh when planning watch orders.
OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol at lower API prices, cutting the cost of using its models in retail software. Astra ranks second on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.
